title: Statutory and Regulatory Compliance Posture for the Inspection Program
capability_statement:
Parsons acknowledges and commits to comply with all statutory and regulatory citations identified in the State Motor Vehicle agency's RFP, including the New Jersey Statutes Annotated (N.J.S.A.) 39:8-2 designation of new-car-dealer sticker vehicles requiring a special replacement-sticker area within the CIF; the procurement framework of P.L.1954, c.48 (C.52:34-6 et seq.) under C.39:8-44 b.(1); the standardized qualification questionnaire required by C.39:8-44 b.(2); the prohibition on State officers/employees involved in award from bidding under C.39:8-44 b.(3); the periodic survey, EPA Administrator/Congressional contact-information, and qualified-MVC-employee employment-offer obligations under C.39:8-44 c.(6) and c.(7); the Chief Administrator oversight authority under C.39:8-44 d.; the early-filing/ADR provisions of C.39:8-44 e. (including N.J.S.59:13-5 and N.J.S.59:13-7); and the comparable-CBA compensation/economic-benefits and successor/assigns provisions of C.39:8-44 g. These compliance commitments are RFP acknowledgements and will be incorporated directly into the proposal response; they do not require past-performance substantiation.

Parsons' general compliance posture supports these acknowledgements. On a comparable I/M Program, Parsons committed to performing all RFP-requested requirements and demonstrated a track record of working with the contracting agency to implement policy, requirement, and regulatory changes - including a seamless transition of more than 8,000 stations to the company's central inspection-data infrastructure and the 2016 revision of OBD inspection-equipment specifications with acceptance testing performed to certify equipment for the program (chunks 1971, 2020). Parsons explicitly recognizes that a contracting agency reserves the right to renegotiate contract terms in the event of needed changes prompted by federal or state legislative requirements or compliance with legally binding court orders, and the company commits to supporting those changes (chunk 2021). Parsons' adaptability, reliability, and adherence to compliance is anchored in proven program execution and consistent regulatory compliance across multiple comparable inspection programs (chunks 2020, 2043).

Parsons routinely operates in environments governed by federal regulations, including the EPA quality-assurance requirements at 40 C.F.R. Section 51.363(a)(1)-(3) and 51.363(b)-(d) for I/M oversight and the 40 C.F.R. Section 51.363(a)(4) requirements for remote visual observation of high-volume stations (chunks 2128, 2133, 2147). Parsons-developed acceptance testing procedures are designed to ensure that all applicable specifications, calibrations, quality-control requirements, and other requirements contained in EPA rules and the contracting agency's I/M regulations are met by all equipment offered for use in the program, with comprehensive ATP scripts developed for every equipment implementation and update (chunks 2091, 2232). Parsons' Vehicle Inspection and Compliance business line has undergone a yearly Service Organization Control (SOC) 2 Type 2 audit since 2018 for security, availability, and confidentiality trust service criteria, with processing-integrity coverage added in 2022 (chunk 2083). Parsons holds quarterly meetings to review security concerns and annual meetings to perform risk analysis as new or revised laws, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines emerge, in accordance with SOC 2 controls (chunk 2084). Oversight and audit procedures - including overt audits, covert audits, remote records audits, remote visual audits, hearings and suspensions, sticker reconciliation, waiver and exemption verification, and report writing/evidence gathering sufficient for building a legal case - are conducted in accordance with the contracting agency's procedures and regulations and produce reports submitted to the agency for appropriate administrative or legal action against violators of state law or agency regulations (chunks 2105, 2106, 2123, 2129, 2138, 2154, 2257, 2266, 2274). Parsons has, on a comparable program, represented the contracting agency in Commonwealth court proceedings - a level of regulatory and legal-process engagement unmatched by competitors (chunk 2274).

differentiators:
- **Dedicated regulatory-change adaptation track record**: On a comparable I/M Program, Parsons has consistently worked with the contracting agency to implement policy, requirement, and regulatory changes, including transitioning more than 8,000 stations to the company's central inspection-data infrastructure in 2012 and revising OBD inspection-equipment specifications in 2016 with full acceptance testing (chunk 1971).
- **Federal I/M regulation execution at scale**: Oversight and audit programs delivered in conformance with 40 C.F.R. Section 51.363(a)(1)-(3), 51.363(b)-(d), and 51.363(a)(4) for remote visual observation, with more than 372,000 overt audits performed (chunks 2128, 2133, 2147).
- **Legal-case-grade evidence collection**: Audit staff are trained in report writing and evidence gathering/documentation necessary for building a legal case, with audit applications providing direct reference to agency regulations to support actionable offenses and improve court-case defenses (chunks 2113, 2123).
- **Direct courtroom representation of the contracting agency**: On a comparable program, Parsons has represented the contracting agency in Commonwealth court proceedings - a depth of regulatory and legal-process engagement explicitly described as unmatched by other vendors (chunk 2274).
- **Continuous third-party compliance attestation**: SOC 2 Type 2 audit completed annually since 2018 (with processing-integrity scope added in 2022) by Parsons' Vehicle Inspection and Compliance business line (chunk 2083).
- **Built-in regulatory-change cadence**: Quarterly security-concern review meetings and annual risk-analysis meetings under SOC 2 controls ensure new or revised laws, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines are systematically incorporated into program operations (chunk 2084).
- **Contract-renegotiation acknowledgement on comparable programs**: Parsons explicitly recognizes the contracting agency's right to renegotiate contract terms in response to federal or state legislative requirements or court-ordered compliance, demonstrating an established and cooperative posture toward regulatory change (chunk 2021).
gap_notes:
- **Most theme-18 requirements are direct statutory acknowledgements, not past-performance claims.** The RFP citations under N.J.S.A. 39:8-2 (R-010), P.L.1954, c.48 / C.52:34-6 et seq. (A-004), C.39:8-44 b.(2) (A-006), C.39:8-44 b.(3) (A-007), C.39:8-44 c.(6) (A-017, A-019), C.39:8-44 c.(7) (A-021), C.39:8-44 d. (A-046), C.39:8-44 e. with N.J.S.59:13-5 and N.J.S.59:13-7 (A-043, A-044), and C.39:8-44 g. (A-031, A-032) are compliance commitments that the proposal must affirm directly. No past-performance citation is required for the acknowledgement itself; capture team should incorporate each citation verbatim into the appropriate proposal section.
- **No evidence of prior Parsons compliance with the specific New Jersey statutes cited.** The available evidence describes federal (40 C.F.R., EPA) and other-state regulatory execution. The proposal must NOT claim prior performance under N.J.S.A./N.J.A.C./C.39:8-44 sections - those are forward-looking compliance commitments only.
- **A-021 (offer of full-time employment to qualified terminated MVC full-time employees) and A-031/A-032 (CBA-comparable compensation/benefits and successor/assigns binding)**: These are HR/labor obligations. The evidence set contains nothing on Parsons' employment-transition practices, CBA-equivalent benefits offers, or successor/assigns clauses from prior contracts. This must be addressed by the proposal team's HR/Legal function and the corporate compensation team; no chunk in this evidence set supports a past-performance citation.
- **R-010 (special replacement-sticker area within the CIF for N.J.S.A. 39:8-2 vehicles)**: The evidence describes sticker reconciliation, sticker disposal, and inspection-sticker tracking on comparable programs (chunks 2129, 2134, 2257, 2262) but does not describe a dedicated CIF replacement-sticker area for new-car-dealer-designated vehicles. Capture team should confirm CIF design and dedicated-area approach with operations.
- **A-019 (written document including EPA Administrator and NJ Congressional member contact info)**: The evidence describes public information and education (I&E) activities, electronic newsletters, physical mailings, and toolbox magnets with QR codes linking to industry regulations (chunks 1970, 2160), but does not describe a written motorist document that includes EPA Administrator and Congressional contact info. This is a content/format compliance commitment that the proposal must affirm; the I&E delivery infrastructure is in place but the specific document content is not evidenced.
- **A-017 (periodic surveys concerning hours and methods of operation)**: Evidence references customer satisfaction surveys, peer-to-peer comparisons of auditor findings, and regular touchpoints (chunks 2256, 2415), but does not describe formal periodic surveys of hours/methods of operation as contemplated by C.39:8-44 c.(6). This is a forward-looking compliance commitment.
- **A-046 (Chief Administrator oversight directives), A-043/A-044 (early filing of dispute notice; ADR/mediation/arbitration under N.J.S.59:13-5 and 59:13-7)**: These are informational/procedural provisions affecting the contracting agency's authority and dispute-resolution rights. They require simple acknowledgement in the proposal; no past-performance evidence is needed.
- **A-006 (standardized qualification questionnaire) and A-004 (P.L.1954, c.48 procurement compliance)**: These are State-side procurement obligations that bind the agency, not the contractor's operations. The proposal should acknowledge that any required questionnaire response will be provided in the standardized form required, and that the contractor accepts award under the procurement framework cited.
- **Voice and naming**: Per instructions, all references to specific past-performance jurisdictions remain neutralized (no Maryland/MVA/VEIP/DoIT). Where evidence chunks reference PennDOT, Pennsylvania, Vermont, Ontario, etc., the synthesized capability statement uses neutral phrasing such as "comparable I/M Program" or "the contracting agency."
